Guides

Portions, texture, and milk

Appetite is a better guide than counting spoonfuls. Milk stays the main drink until the first birthday.

Findings

Start with a few teaspoons, then follow your baby’s lead. A few spoonfuls one day and a whole bowl the next can both be normal.
Until 12 months, milk is still most of the diet. Food is there for iron and practice. It doesn’t need to replace milk feeds on a schedule you make up.
By eight or nine months, textures should be moving on. You can offer water from an open cup with meals. Not juice.

How much food?

The first meals are as much about practice as nutrition: one to three teaspoons, once a day, building up to two and then three meals. By the end of the first year, many children have three meals and two snacks, though portions still vary hugely from child to child and day to day.

Pushing those last few spoonfuls teaches a child to ignore feeling full. So does using food as a reward, or as comfort for every upset. There’s more on sharing responsibility on the meals page: you decide what to offer, your child decides how much to eat.

Where milk fits

Keep offering breast milk or formula on demand alongside meals. There’s no need to drop a milk feed the day solids start. As the first birthday approaches, food provides more of the iron, and milk feeds often settle into morning, evening, and maybe one more.

After 12 months, drinking well over 400 ml of milk a day is a common reason a toddler won’t eat. Offer water with meals. Sipping from a bottle all day can also leave milk pooling on the teeth.

Texture and cups

Smooth food at six months, mash and soft strips by eight or nine, and chopped family food by twelve is a good rough path. Some babies move faster, some slower. The real risk is a child who reaches one still on thin purée and then refuses lumps.

Offer sips of water from an open or free-flow cup at meals so your baby gets to practise drinking. Juice, even diluted, isn’t a drink for babies. The American Academy of Pediatrics advises no juice before 12 months.
